claims.text: An AlCoCrFeNi-family HEA is a suitable coating material for a Cu substrate.
Controlled sputtering of an HEA onto Cu will produce a strongly adherent coating.
An HEA coating on Cu will provide a wear-resistant surface layer.
A thin interdiffused interface between Cu and the HEA enhances metallurgical bonding.
The initial Cu substrate has a smooth, uncoated surface.
The HEA coating is to be deposited by physical vapor deposition using sputtering.
Varying substrate temperature during sputtering can be used to control the Cu/HEA interface.
A controlled inert atmosphere and an appropriate substrate temperature promote limited interdiffusion without overheating Cu.
Partial atomic interdiffusion creates a nanometer-scale interfacial layer between the Cu substrate and HEA coating.
Controlled interdiffusion, potentially including transitional phases, produces metallurgical bonding at the Cu/HEA interface.
Metallurgical bonding anchors the hard HEA layer to the Cu matrix.
The sputtered HEA coating will improve adhesion on Cu as measured by scratch and indentation tests.
The sputtered HEA coating will improve Cu wear resistance relative to uncoated Cu.
Uncoated Cu has lower wear resistance and poorer surface-protection performance than HEA-coated Cu.
Excessively high deposition temperature can cause excessive interdiffusion at the Cu/HEA interface.
An incompatible HEA composition can produce brittle intermetallic compounds that deteriorate coating adhesion and performance.
The optimal deposition-temperature range and HEA composition for minimizing detrimental Cu/HEA interfacial reactions are not yet specified and require experiment.
